To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

synchronous checkpointing with load redistribution is more effective for systems where the failure rate is high, the speedup of parallel algorithms is low, and the failure-free execution times are large.

1) synchronous checkpointing with load redistribution can significantly improve the performance of parallel programs, 2) the performance gain increases as a function of both the number of nodes and the speedup function of the parallel program, and 3) the performance gain is maximized for a given parallel program when the number of nodes is equal to or less than the number of checkpoints
The optimum checkpoint interval for synchronous checkpointing is inversely proportional to the failure rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of determining the optimum checkpoint interval for a distributed computing system in the presence of failures.
the problem of determining the best checkpoint interval in a distributed computing system.
the performance of synchronous, distributed checkpointing in a parallel computing environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimum checkpoint interval is a function of the failure-free performance, the speedup function, the failure rate, and the number of nodes.
synchronous checkpointing is advantageous when the checkpoint interval is small and load redistribution is not advantageous when the checkpoint intervals are small.
synchronous checkpointing with load redistribution is the most advantageous technique for distributed computing systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the optimal checkpoint interval is a function of the speedup function and the number of processors.
the performance of a distributed computing system is improved when checkpointing is used.
we have developed a general model for distributed systems and have applied it to a specific parallel algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
load redistribution is not necessarily a panacea for improving the performance of a checkpoint/restart system.
synchronous checkpointing with load redistribution is not always the most efficient way to reduce the mean time to failure of a distributed computing system.
synchronous checkpointing with load redistribution can be advantageous for a broad range of system configurations.
